But let's assume it's not worse case scenario, Let's just say, the system of logistics broke down. And, fuck it, let's assume barbarian neighbors aren't an issue, just to give you a chance in this hypothetical situation.

So, we are talking no food, water, or energy apart from what you've previously stored.

You aren't going to be able to store very much water simply because it's heavy. 1 Liter = 1 Kilogram. 1 Cubic Meter is 1 metric ton (1000 Kg) So living in an apartment is going to limit the amount of water you can store because the floor isn't going to safely support the weight. So, at best, you'll have about 1 month or so of water if all you are doing is sustaining your life and not doing things like using it to clean or supporting family.

You can probably store enough food for a year, but food is worthless when you have no water. So, only store as much food as you can support it with water. (1 month of water = 1 month of food)

Then we come to energy, In the city, you really can't do much about this. Electricity and gas rely on the grid and you can't very well start a fire with wood or coal without a fireplace. If you have a fireplace you might be able to hold out longer than a month provided you can scrounge up wood (which is unlikely) and it's doubtful that you have room to store a cord of wood (in addition to the water and food)

Let's say you live in a 2 bedroom apartment. You are going to be sacrificing the use of that whole bedroom for 1 month of living IF things eventually go bad.
